name: InfoBento
description: Solar-powered B&W eInk decorator for kitchen counters, desks, and shelves. Enclosure sized to fit the GDEH0576T81 panel closely (~14x11cm) with a Good Display GDEH0576T81 5.76" 920x680 198-DPI eInk panel (SSD2677 driver) that nearly fills the front face. Monolithic white housing, solar panel on the upper back, body-as-stand with ~12-15° tilt. Two tilt switches detect orientation for auto-rotate. Designed to survive a 4-foot drop. Configure once on a web page; refreshes 1-2x/day on solar power. $30-40 target via Kickstarter. Renderer produces 2-bit grayscale (4-level) framebuffers with antialiased TTF fonts (Inter) and configurable rounded box borders. Color deferred to v2.

artifacts.name: Grayscale Elegance
artifacts.statement: Four shades — black, dark gray, light gray, white — used with intention. Every tone earns its place.
artifacts.description: V1 ships monochrome with 4-level grayscale (2-bit per pixel). The hardware supports this natively at no extra cost. The four tones create a clear visual hierarchy: black for hero data and primary text, dark gray for secondary content and dividers, light gray for labels and metadata, white for background. Anti-aliased fonts become possible — 2-bit grayscale text is crisper than 1-bit at the same DPI, especially for the 5x7 small font where staircase aliasing is visible. The constraint is still tight enough to feel intentional: four shades, not a gradient. Think newspaper print, not a photograph.
artifacts.source: Round 11 direction (2026-04-23). The GDEH0576T81 (SSD2677 driver) supports 4 grayscale natively. Anti-aliased TTF font rendering (Inter via opentype.js) is the primary motivation — free visual quality improvement from hardware already being purchased.
examples: Hero font in black, section labels in light gray — instant hierarchy without layout gymnastics
Anti-aliased Inter TTF font: edge pixels rendered in dark/light gray via opentype.js rasterization

More than two font sizes (creates visual noise — grayscale is for tone, not for adding complexity)

artifacts.description: All 18 box types use free data sources or local computation. Weather, forecast, forecast3d, sunrise/sunset, and air quality use Open-Meteo (free, no key). Quotes use the api.quotable.kurokeita.dev mirror (free, no auth). Horoscope uses api-ninjas (free), joke uses JokeAPI (free), on-this-day uses Wikipedia (free). Stocks uses Yahoo Finance (free, no key). Date, moon, countdown, progress, QR, text, habits, and calendar are pure local computation or user input. Quote/joke/horoscope additionally fall back to a bundled ~50KB local set on upstream failure. No user should need to create an account anywhere to use the product.
artifacts.source: User research — friction in setup kills adoption for consumer hardware

artifacts.description: The web editor at infobento.com is the only configuration surface. Configuration lives in browser localStorage with JSON import/export. artifacts.source: Round 10 counter pivot follow-on session (2026-04-22). Founder explicitly chose this scope after walking back the calendar / real-time-ish use case that would have justified native apps.

artifacts.title: Open Question Decisions — Rounds 1-5
artifacts.body:
Decisions made during planning sessions:

## Round 1 (resolved)
- MVP box types: weather (Open-Meteo), quote (ZenQuotes), countdown, QR, text — all free, no auth
- Web framework: Hono + Vite (same-port architecture like phasebot)
- Web app private during dev, co-hosted with tiles- and webmap.dev later
- Version starts at 0.1.0

## Round 2 (resolved)
1. MVP scope: text + countdown + weather first (proves pipeline), then QR + quote
2. Weather location: Open-Meteo geocoding API, user types city name
3. Config persistence: localStorage + JSON export/import (no server state)
4. Refresh scheduling: web UI sets schedule, phone app executes it, device responds
5. Design language: clean/minimal with sharp borders, receipt-style typography
6. Name: InfoBento (confirmed final)

## Round 3 (resolved)
1. Implementation order: text -> countdown -> weather -> QR -> quote
2. Mobile web layout: stack vertically (preview on top, config below)
3. Font: embedded small fixed-width bitmap font (5x7 or 6x8 pixel, embedded-systems style)
4. QR sizing: larger allocation — half display height or more, not constrained to a thin box
5. Name confirmed: InfoBento is final

## Round 4 — Market & Positioning (resolved 2026-04-21)
1. Primary user: Daily Glancer (the founder)
2. Distribution: Kickstarter
3. Price target: $30 (bumped from $25 after BOM analysis)
4. Hardware: ESP32-C3 + eInk + battery w/ solar drip charger + solar panel kickstand (details in issue #22)
5. Competitive positioning: resolved — 'See what matters. Skip the spiral.' anti-phone angle

## Round 5 — Form Factor & Interaction Model (resolved 2026-04-21)
1. Form factor: clamshell with 180-degree hinge. Two halves: eInk display + solar panel
2. Primary mode: MagSafe-mounted on back of iPhone, eInk facing out. User flips phone to peek.
3. Secondary mode: standing on counter/desk, hinge open, solar panel aimed at window, display facing room
4. Size constraint: must fit on iPhone 15 Pro back (146.6 x 70.6mm), may partially cover camera
6. Interaction model: zero interaction with InfoBento itself. No buttons, no app to open.
7. Refresh rate: must increase in phone-mounted mode (minutes, not hours) vs standalone (1-2x/day)
8. MVP stays simple (weather, countdown, text, QR, quote). Authenticated integrations (calendar, messages, smart home) come post-MVP.
9. Kitchen counter is the hero Kickstarter scenario. Phone-mounted is the daily use case.

## Round 6 — Phase Scoping (resolved 2026-04-21)

### Phase 2 (core) — COMPLETE
1. Zod validation with field-level error paths (validateBentoConfig)
2. Each box renderer handles its own data fetching/parsing
3. Horizontal subdivision (split: 'left' | 'right') implemented
4. Display resolution: 128x296 portrait, abstracted via constants

### Phase 3 (renderer) — COMPLETE
1. All 5 box renderers with hero font + whitespace layout + icons
2. Spleen 8x16 hero font + 5x7 data font + 7x7 icon set
3. CUT: dithering (no grayscale sources), frame diffing (no firmware yet)
4. Renderer stays pure — API fetching handled by web/api packages

### Phase 4 (API) — COMPLETE
1. Structured error responses via Zod validation with field-level paths
2. frameToPng re-exported from api package
3. Health endpoint reads version from package.json dynamically
4. Box-types endpoint lists only 5 implemented types
5. /api/quote proxy for ZenQuotes (bypasses CORS)

### Phase 5 (web) — COMPLETE
1. Vanilla JS with reactive state, D/P display toggle
2. Client-side 1-bit canvas renderer, localStorage, import/export JSON
3. Live weather fetch (Open-Meteo), random quote (/api/quote proxy)
4. Mobile responsive CSS, empty states, input validation
5. 1-bit icon set in box headers
6. Deployed to infobento.com (nginx + systemd)

## Still open (hardware) — updated Round 11
- ~~Hinge sourcing~~ — removed (no hinge in counter-only device)
- ~~Background BLE on iOS~~ — removed (Wi-Fi direct, no phone app)
- ~~eInk partial refresh / BLE tuning~~ — removed (no phone-mounted mode)
- B&W panel sourcing (#47): golden-ratio, high DPI, bento scale
- Tilt switch selection (#48): component, GPIO, mounting
- SCAD enclosure (#50): bento dimensions, ≤3mm bezel
- BOM at $30-40: B&W panel (~$25-35) makes target realistic

## Resolved (no longer open)
- BLE version: 5.0 (ESP32-C3 supports it natively)
- Battery capacity: ~100mAh target (352035 form factor)
- Anti-aliasing: not possible at 1-bit, solved with purpose-designed Spleen 8x16 font
- Hinge: 180-degree standard friction, book-style along 70.6mm short edge (reduced from 320-degree)
- MagSafe: full N52 ring on solar half (M-side), Qi coil inside ring
- Price: $30
- Thickness: ~8mm folded (accepted)
- Display panel: glass (not flex)
- Display resolution: 128x296 portrait
- Battery placement: solar half — avoids grip flex stress on LiPo cell. Power through hinge FPC (2 wires, ~100mA). Display half has no battery.
- Folded thickness: ~7.2mm (3.2mm display + 4.0mm solar) (standard 2.9-inch panel rotated). Codebase updated.
- Physical modes: closed (0° phone-mounted), peek (90°), counter (~100° solar charging)
- Solar charging: counter mode only, not phone-mounted

## Round 7 — Hardware Design Decisions (resolved 2026-04-21)
1. Glass eInk panel (not flex) — flex adds $7-10/unit for 0.9mm savings, not worth it at this stage
2. Accept ~8mm folded thickness — position as 'slim enough for a back pocket' (comparable to MagSafe Battery Pack at 11.3mm, thinner than most phone cases with card holders)
3. Price target bumped from $25 to $30 — BOM analysis showed charging subsystem ($13-18) + hinge ($4-30) + display ($5-8) leaves no margin at $25
4. See issue #22 for full hardware design exploration and proposed component layout

## Round 8 — Physical Modes & Hinge Hardening (2026-04-21)

### Four-surface labeling
The device has 2 halves x 2 sides = 4 distinct surfaces:
- D = eInk display (outer face of display half) — phone-mounted content
- P = eInk display (inner face of display half) — counter/peek content
- S = Solar panel (inner face of solar half)
- M = MagSafe + Qi (outer face of solar half — magnets, coil)
When closed: D faces out, M faces phone, P and S sandwiched inside.

### Three operating modes (180-degree hinge)
1. CLOSED (0°) — Phone mounted. M touches phone (MagSafe holds), D faces outward. Display visible on phone back. Solar not charging.
2. PEEK (90°) — Quick glance. Solar half flat, display half vertical. L-shape. User opens device 90° to read display while phone is on desk.
3. COUNTER (~100°) — Solar charging. M-side down as base, S faces up toward light, D faces user at angle. Standalone on counter/desk.

### Decisions
1. Peek mode is 90° (not 10-20° as originally discussed) — clear L-shape, display fully visible
2. Counter mode: solar half is the base (M-side down), solar panel faces up for charging
3. Simultaneous mount+stand is NOT a use case — device is either on phone or on counter
4. Solar charging only happens in counter mode (not phone-mounted)
5. FLAT (180°) exists mechanically but is not a useful operating mode — storage/transport only

### Dual display — DECIDED: yes, same size (Variant A)
- Two 2.9-inch 128x296 eInk panels back-to-back on display half PCB
- D (outer): real-time phone-mounted content, partial refresh every 2-5 min
- P (inner): ambient counter/peek content, full refresh 1-2x/day
- GPIO budget: 10 of 13 pins, 3 spare. Shared SPI + RST.
- Thickness: 3.2mm display half (improved from 4.4mm single-display)
- BOM: +$5-8 for second panel
- No re-render on mode switch — each display holds its own frame
- Software: extend BentoConfig with displayId: 'D' | 'P', two independent configs
- Display resolution confirmed: 128x296 portrait. Codebase updated.

artifacts.label: REQ-007
artifacts.statement: QR code box type gets a larger vertical allocation (approximately half display height) to ensure scannability

artifacts.rationale: A QR code in a 35px-tall box would be too small to scan reliably. Larger allocation ensures real-world utility.

artifacts.name: Two-Font Bitmap System
artifacts.statement: TrueType font rendering via Inter (OFL) with opentype.js — configurable body size (8-42px), hero size derived proportionally — no system font dependencies
artifacts.description: The renderer uses Inter (OFL-licensed TrueType font) via opentype.js for all text. Body font size is user-configurable (8-42px, default 38px); hero size is derived proportionally (bodySize * 2.6). Anti-aliased at 2-bit grayscale depth via scanline TTF rasterization. Dynamic FontMetrics system computes all spacing, padding, and line heights from the chosen body size. Two visual weights — hero (bold) and body (regular) — create clear hierarchy.
artifacts.source: Font evolution: 5x7 bitmap (v0.1) → Spleen 8x16 bitmap (v0.4) → Inter TTF via opentype.js (v0.7.0). TTF rendering enables configurable font sizes and proper kerning.
examples: Inter Bold hero: '62F', '9:00', '14 days' at user-chosen size
Inter Regular body: 'WEATHER', 'Partly Cloudy', 'H:68 L:55'
Two weights + configurable size create clear hierarchy
counterExamples: System fonts rendered via Canvas API
Fixed bitmap fonts with no size flexibility
Three or more font sizes (creates visual noise)

artifacts.name: Rendering Pipeline (v0.4.0+)
artifacts.description: Full rendering pipeline: BentoConfig (Zod-validated) -> layout (vertical + horizontal split, configurable padding) -> Inter TTF fonts + SDF rounded borders + 14x14 icons -> draw -> 156,400-byte frame buffer (920x680, 2-bit grayscale). 18 box types with content-aware height allocation. Web editor with font size, corner radius, and padding controls, in-place box type switcher, and add-box chip rail. Deployed to infobento.com.
artifacts.scope: Core types with Zod validation, layout engine (920x680, configurable padding, horizontal split, content-aware height hints), Inter TTF fonts via opentype.js, SDF rounded borders, 14x14 icons, 18 box renderers, single-column web editor with font/corner/padding controls + server-rendered PNG preview + localStorage v2, API with structured errors, passkey + Apple/Google OAuth auth, deployed
knownLimitations: No center alignment in text rendering
Maximum 10 boxes enforced by layout truncation (dynamic based on font size)
Weather and quote data fetched client-side only (no server-side caching)
No firmware yet — software demo only (firmware tracked in #39, #48, #49)

artifacts.description: Original BentoBox interface used a single optional BoxConfig field, allowing { type: weather, config: { type: text } } without type error. Fixed with discriminated union (TextBentoBox | UnconfiguredBentoBox).

artifacts.label: REQ-008
artifacts.statement: Users can see a live PNG preview of their bento layout before syncing to device
artifacts.source: Implementation need — raw binary frame buffer is not human-viewable; preview is essential for the web config experience

artifacts.label: REQ-009
artifacts.statement: V1 ships monochrome with 4-level grayscale (2-bit framebuffer: black, dark gray, light gray, white). No color eInk.
artifacts.source: Round 11 direction (2026-04-23), revised after confirming all candidate panels (GDEY075T7, GDEQ0426T82, GDEH0576T81, etc.) natively support 4 grayscale levels at zero additional BOM cost. Grayscale enables anti-aliased fonts, visual hierarchy via gray tones, and smoother renderings.
artifacts.rationale: The GDEH0576T81 (SSD2677 driver) supports 4 grayscale natively. Using 2-bit instead of 1-bit costs nothing in BOM or refresh time and enables: (1) anti-aliased TTF font rendering for crisper text at 198 DPI, (2) light gray for secondary labels vs black for primary data, (3) dark gray for SDF-antialiased rounded box borders, (4) smoother moon phase and progress bar fills. Color eInk (Spectra 6, ACeP) remains deferred to v2.

artifacts.label: REQ-010
artifacts.statement: Device enclosure (~14×11cm) fits the GDEH0576T81 panel closely with minimal bezel, golden-ratio display (1.618:1 target aspect ratio)
artifacts.source: Round 11 direction (2026-04-23). The product is called InfoBento — it should feel like a bento box. Golden ratio (φ) produces the most naturally pleasing proportions for an information display. Closest stock panel: 7.5" at 5:3 (1.667:1, 3% from φ). Custom panels at volume can hit 1.618:1 exactly.
artifacts.rationale: Size and proportion are core to the product identity. The bento box metaphor — compartmentalized, balanced, portable — should be reflected in the physical object. At ~14×11cm the enclosure fits the GDEH0576T81 panel module (125.4×99.5mm) closely with minimal bezel, keeping the device compact enough to sit on a counter without dominating the surface while remaining large enough for comfortable reading from across a room.

artifacts.label: REQ-011
artifacts.statement: Display must be high DPI (≥200 DPI target, ≥124 DPI minimum) and nearly fill the enclosure (≤4mm visible bezel)
artifacts.source: Round 11 direction (2026-04-23). High DPI ensures crisp text at glance distance. Minimal bezel maximizes the 'all-screen' aesthetic — the display IS the device from the front.
artifacts.rationale: At 1-bit, DPI directly determines text sharpness — there is no anti-aliasing to compensate for low resolution. Minimal bezel makes the device look like a floating sheet of paper rather than a gadget with a screen. Stock 7.5" panels (124 DPI) are acceptable for launch; ≥200 DPI is the target for volume production (custom panel order at 5K+ units).

artifacts.label: REQ-012
artifacts.statement: Device detects orientation via two tilt switches and auto-rotates the display layout (landscape, portrait, inverted landscape, inverted portrait)
artifacts.source: Round 11 direction (2026-04-23). Two mechanical ball-in-tube tilt switches mounted at 90° to each other on two GPIO pins. Zero standby current, ~$0.10 total BOM, no I2C bus needed. Each switch triggers a GPIO interrupt on state change; firmware reads both pins to determine one of four orientations and re-renders the layout if changed.
artifacts.rationale: Users will naturally stand the device in both orientations. Without auto-rotation, the display would be sideways — a dealbreaker for a glance display. Tilt switches are simpler and cheaper than a discrete IMU (LIS2DW12, BMA400) while fully meeting the requirement. Zero standby current stays well within the solar power budget. Four-orientation detection (2 switches × 2 states) covers all practical placements.

artifacts.name: Solar-Powered Counter Display
artifacts.statement: InfoBento is a bento-box-sized counter device — single high-DPI B&W eInk display on the front, solar panel on the upper portion of the back, body-as-stand. No hinge, no MagSafe, no kickstand. Tilt switches detect orientation for auto-rotate.
artifacts.description: The device is a single white-housed body sized to fit the GDEH0576T81 panel closely (~14×11cm), with a golden-ratio B&W eInk panel that nearly fills the front face (≤3mm bezel target). Front: high-DPI B&W eInk panel recessed into the bezel rim so the rim shields the glass on a face-down drop. Back-upper: solar panel cavity (~70x100mm) for indirect window-light harvesting. Back-lower: ESP32-C3 + battery + tilt switches + grip area. Two mechanical tilt switches at 90° on two GPIO pins detect orientation changes (zero standby current, ~$0.10 BOM) and fire hardware interrupts so the layout re-renders in the correct rotation — landscape when flat, portrait when stood on its short edge, plus both inverted orientations. The back surface tilts ~12-15° relative to the front so the device naturally angles upward. Designed to survive a 4-foot drop. Refreshes once or twice a day on solar power; counter-only, no phone-mounted mode.
artifacts.source: Round 10 counter pivot (2026-04-22). Replaces the prior dual-display MagSafe clamshell concept after user-class fit analysis showed the clamshell was trying to serve two products at once and paying for it with BOM, thickness, and the iOS background BLE risk.
examples: Kitchen counter: device leans slightly back on its own footprint, display angled toward standing viewer, solar panel catching window light from the upper back surface
Desk: device sits next to a monitor, crisp B&W quote and weather visible from working distance
Shelf: device functions as ambient decor — quote, countdown, weather — no plug, no cable
Dropped onto hardwood from 4 feet: bumper compresses, edges absorb impact, glass intact

artifacts.title: Hardware Platform
artifacts.body:
## Counter device platform (rewritten 2026-04-23 for Round 11 B&W + bento direction)

Monolithic counter device (~14x11cm, sized to fit the GDEH0576T81 panel closely). White housing, ≤3mm bezel, golden-ratio B&W eInk display, no hinge, no MagSafe, no kickstand. Panel SKU pending #47.

### Front
- Single B&W eInk panel — Good Display GDEH0576T81 (5.76", 920x680, 198 DPI, SSD2677 driver, active area 117.7x87.0mm)
- 2-bit grayscale rendering (4 levels: white, light gray, dark gray, black — REQ-009)
- Bezel: ≤3mm visible on all four sides (REQ-011) — display nearly fills the front face
- Display recess: deep enough that the bezel rim shields the glass on a face-down drop

### Back-upper
- Solar panel cavity, ~70x100mm amorphous-Si, 0.22mm thick
- Mounted on the upper third of the back surface so it catches indirect window light when the device sits on a counter
- AEM10941 solar harvesting IC drives charging

### Back-lower
- ESP32-C3 (Wi-Fi 4 + BLE 5) — locked 2026-04-22; BLE radio reserved unused for v2 bridge mode
- LiPo battery: ~100mAh target (B&W refresh is ~2-3s, much less power than color)
- MCP73831 LiPo charger
- **Two tilt switches** (REQ-012): ball-in-tube type, mounted at 90° to each other on two GPIO pins. Zero standby current. Detect 4 orientations: landscape, portrait, inverted landscape, inverted portrait. Fire GPIO interrupts for auto-rotate.
- Provides grip area when device is picked up
- **Recessed pinhole reset:** ~2mm diameter, centered, recessed into the bumper layer. Press with paperclip for 5s = factory reset (clears Wi-Fi credentials and re-enters AP mode). Documented on a small label on the back. Only physical affordance on the device.

### Industrial design
- Enclosure: ~140x110mm body (REQ-010), sized to fit the GDEH0576T81 panel (125.4x99.5mm module) closely with minimal bezel
- White housing (color locked, founder decision)
- Edge-radiused corners (~4mm radius) to disperse impact energy
- Back surface tilts ~12-15° relative to front so device naturally angles its display upward when placed on a flat counter — body-as-stand, no separate kickstand mechanism
- Soft polymer bumper layer between the eInk glass and the housing rim (silicone vs TPU vs over-molded TPE — choice pending)
- Designed to survive a 4-foot drop onto a hard surface (drop-test protocol in #36 / `docs/hardware/DROP-TEST.md`)

### Connectivity (locked 2026-04-22 — see `docs/hardware/CONNECTIVITY.md`)
- **Wi-Fi direct + PWA-only.** Device makes outbound HTTPS calls to the cloud API. No companion phone app for v1.
- **First-time setup:** captive-portal flow. Device boots in AP mode, advertises `InfoBento-XXXX` SSID, user joins, OS auto-launches browser to setup page, user enters home Wi-Fi credentials, device joins home network.
- **Recovery:** pinhole reset (above) for dead-device cases.
- **v2 path:** BLE radio is unused but available. Native iOS/Android apps + BLE bridge can ship later as a firmware update + companion app, no hardware refresh needed.

### Cloud hosting (locked 2026-04-22)
- **DigitalOcean droplet** ($6/mo tier; co-tenant with tiles- and webmap.dev — marginal cost ~$1-2/mo for InfoBento)
- **Cloudflare** in front (free tier) for DNS + CDN + DDoS + TLS edge
- **Caddy** on the droplet for TLS termination + reverse proxy + Let's Encrypt auto-cert
- **Hono on Node** as the API runtime (already shipping; `packages/api`)
- **OTA firmware files** served from `/var/www/firmware/*.bin` on the droplet — no object storage needed at this scale
- Sizing: $6 tier handles ~10K devices with several orders of magnitude of headroom
- Migration path open: Hono runs on Cloudflare Workers / Vercel / Bun / Deno without code changes

### GPIO allocation (preliminary)
- SPI: MOSI, SCLK, CS, DC, BUSY, RST for the single panel — 6 pins
- Tilt switches: 2 GPIO pins (with interrupts)
- Battery ADC: 1 pin
- Wi-Fi/BLE: handled by MCU module
- Total: ~9 pins used, comfortable headroom on ESP32-C3

### Thickness
- Estimated 8-12mm depending on chosen panel and battery — single body, no fold
- The device is decorator-class (sits on a counter), not pocket-class — thickness is not a hero spec

### BOM target: $30-40 retail (improved by B&W)
- B&W eInk panel: $25-35 (stock 7.5"); custom at volume potentially lower
- ESP32-C3: $2-4
- LiPo battery + AEM10941 + MCP73831: $5-7
- Solar panel: $2-4
- Tilt switches (x2): $0.10
- Housing (injection-molded white plastic at volume): $3-6
- Bumper (silicone or TPU): $1-2
- Assembly + packaging: $3-5
- Subtotal range: ~$41-63. $30-40 retail achievable at volume with aggressive sourcing.
- **vs color:** B&W saves $15-30 on the panel vs Spectra 6/ACeP, making the $30 price point realistic.

### What's gone vs the clamshell concept
- Second eInk panel and its driver lines
- Hinge, hinge FPC, hinge sourcing risk
- MagSafe N52 magnet ring and Qi receiver IC
- iOS background BLE as a project risk
- Dual-PCB / through-hinge power routing
- Color eInk (Spectra 6 / ACeP) — deferred to v2

artifacts.title: Market & Distribution
artifacts.body:
**Canonical Kickstarter draft lives at `docs/kickstarter-copy.md`.** This note holds high-level positioning, competitive landscape, and value-prop reasoning. Issue #38 tracks the copy through to launch. Updated 2026-04-23 for Round 11 (B&W + bento form factor).

## Positioning (revised 2026-04-23 for B&W + bento direction)
- Price target: $30-40 retail (final number gated on panel choice in #47)
- Distribution: Kickstarter
- Timeline: when the prototype hardware exists (Phase 4)
- Primary buyer: Desk Decorator and Gift Giver. Daily Glancer is secondary.

## Competitive landscape
- Phone widgets / lock screen: free, but still require pick-up + wake. Not a counter object.
- Smartwatch complications: on wrist, small, subscription-heavy. Different surface entirely.
- Tidbyt / Vestaboard / LaMetric: $150-300, LED dot-matrix, glows, animates, requires power cable. InfoBento: paper-like B&W eInk, still, solar-powered, ten times cheaper.
- DIY eInk frames (Waveshare, LILYGO, Inkplate): $25-80 unassembled, no polish, requires coding. InfoBento is the assembled, polished, bento-box-shaped version.
- Digital photo frames: $40-200, require power cables, no contextual content.
- TRMNL: closest competitor — B&W eInk, developer-focused. InfoBento differentiates on form factor (golden ratio, bento-sized, solar-powered, auto-rotate) and zero-code setup.

## InfoBento's gap
- Paper-like B&W crispness at high DPI — reads like print, not a screen
- Bento-box form factor with golden-ratio proportions — looks intentional, not generic
- Auto-rotate via tilt switches — landscape on counter, portrait on shelf
- Solar-powered, no cable, no plug, no batteries to replace
- No accounts, no subscriptions, no app required
- $30-40 vs $150+ for smart displays

## Kickstarter hero scenario
- Kitchen counter, morning light, crisp B&W weather and quote visible from across the room while the user makes coffee. Solar panel on the upper back catches the window. The golden-ratio proportions make it look like a small piece of art.

## Value proposition — B&W bento revision 2026-04-23
- Tagline: See what matters. Skip the spiral.
- Angle: a calm paper-like surface for your counter. The information you check most often, rendered in sharp black ink on white, on its own, on sunlight.
- New competitive framing vs Tidbyt: 'Tidbyt glows. InfoBento reads.' — a paper-like B&W surface vs an LED dot matrix. Stillness is the feature.
- Price justification: less than a smart display, more polished than DIY, shaped like its namesake.
- The bento metaphor: compartmentalized information, balanced layout, portable config.

## Kickstarter pitch (B&W bento revision 2026-04-23)
Most of the time, your phone holds your whole life beautifully. But sometimes you just want to know if it's going to rain, or how many days until your trip, without opening five apps and resurfacing twenty minutes later. InfoBento is a bento-box-shaped eInk display that sits on your counter, your desk, or a shelf. Weather, the moon phase, a countdown, a quote — all visible at a glance from across the room, in crisp black ink on paper-white. The golden-ratio proportions make it look like a small piece of art. Stand it landscape or portrait — it auto-rotates. The solar panel on the back catches indirect light through the window. No cables, no account, no batteries to swap, no buttons to press. Configure your boxes once on a web page and it just works — for months, silently, on sunlight. At $30, InfoBento isn't a smart home device or a screen competing for your attention. It's a calm surface that reads like paper — what matters, where it matters, and nothing else.

artifacts.title: eInk display design research — layout patterns (addressed)
artifacts.description:
Research across Tidbyt, Watchy, TRMNL, thermal printer art, and eInk phone accessories (YotaPhone, InkCase, HiSense) yielded consistent design principles for small 1-bit displays:

1. ONE DOMINANT ELEMENT — a single large hero element (time, temperature) taking 40-50% of height reads best. Cramming too much kills legibility.
2. TWO FONT SIZES MAX — large hero + small data. No medium. The contrast jump IS the hierarchy.
3. WHITESPACE BEATS BORDERS — generous padding between sections feels cleaner than 1px borders around everything. Current renderer over-uses borders.
4. RECEIPT-STYLE LAYOUT — label left-aligned, value right-aligned, monospace. Horizontal rules as dividers.
5. 3-4 DATA ITEMS MAX — rotate screens for more info rather than crowding one frame.
6. STATIC > INTERACTIVE — eInk phone accessories that tried to be mini-Android (YotaPhone, HiSense) disappointed users. Single-purpose static frames (InkCase clock faces) worked best.
7. NO TOUCH REQUIRED — designs assuming eInk touch input universally failed. Treat the back as display-only.

The current renderer treats all boxes identically (border + uppercase label + dotted divider + wrapped text). The research points toward differentiated visual treatment per box type as the next rendering improvement.
artifacts.evidence: Web research: Tidbyt review (macwright.com), Watchy docs (sqfmi), TRMNL (trmnl.com), YotaPhone review (Engadget, Phone Scoop), InkCase (Kickstarter), thermal-sans-mono (GitHub)
artifacts.recommendation: Implement hero font size for primary data (weather temp, countdown number). Reduce border usage — use whitespace gaps instead. Differentiate box renderers visually by type. Consider screen rotation (2-3 states cycling) as an alternative to cramming 6 boxes.

artifacts.body:
Web editor changes that landed this session, in support of the demo's role as the Kickstarter campaign's interactive proof point.

## Layout — dual-display always visible
- Replaced the `D (Phone)` / `P (Counter)` toggle with a 2x2 CSS grid: previews on top (Outer left, Inner right), editors below in the same alignment.
- 'Outer' / 'Inner' labels (was `D` / `P`) make the public-vs-private mental model explicit at a glance.
- Header chrome cleaned up: title `InfoBento`, `EDITOR vX.Y.Z` badge with version stamped from package.json at build time, single right-aligned `Menu` dropdown for Import / Export JSON.
- Mobile (≤720px) stacks all four panels vertically: Outer Preview, Inner Preview, Outer Editor, Inner Editor.
- Live preview was clipping to the top ~22% of the layout because `#eink-display` was hard-sized to 240×200 with overflow:hidden while the canvas painted at 384×888 (CSS legacy from before the canvas approach). Resolved by sizing the panel from the canvas via CSS variables (`--eink-w` / `--eink-h`) published by the renderer.

## Geocoding — Nominatim (OpenStreetMap)
- Weather and 3hr Forecast boxes now resolve free-form locations via Nominatim instead of Open-Meteo's geocoder.
- Open-Meteo couldn't handle 'Portland, OR' (no admin filter) or landmarks like 'Mt. St. Helens'. Nominatim handles both naturally — addresses, towns, regions, peaks.
- Open-Meteo still serves the actual weather/hourly data; only geocoding moved.

## New box type — 3hr Forecast
- Editor type with the same UX as Weather: location field, auto-fetch on mount, status string under the input.
- Renders as three rows of `time | tempF | condition` from Open-Meteo's hourly endpoint, slicing the next 3 hours from current.
- Adds a 6th MVP box type (was 5: text, countdown, weather, qr, quote). Updates REQ-004 implicitly — 6 box types now.

## Consent dialog
- First-load modal covering both Privacy and Terms, single Accept button, persisted in localStorage with a CONSENT_VERSION integer so future material policy changes can re-prompt.
- Content grounded in 'Free by Default' and 'Pure Function Architecture' principles: no accounts, no tracking, no telemetry, third-party calls (Open-Meteo / Nominatim / ZenQuotes) named explicitly. Tagline 'See what matters. Skip the spiral.' as subtitle.

## Display dimensions — corrected to spec
- Codebase had been shipping 128×296 (the panel-native portrait orientation). Project documentation and CLAUDE.md called for 240×200 (landscape, after rotation). Constants updated to 240×200.
- Tests refactored to derive frame buffer size and dimensions from `DISPLAY_WIDTH` / `DISPLAY_HEIGHT` / `DEFAULT_FRAME_BYTES` instead of hard-coded literals (4736, 128, 296). Future spec change is now a one-line edit in `constants.ts`.
- Hardware notes elsewhere in this project.json still say `128x296 portrait` in several places (Hardware Platform note, dual-display section of Round 8). Code-vs-doc mismatch to resolve as a follow-up before campaign launch.

## Tagline + pitch tone (revised 2026-04-22)
- Tagline changed from 'See less. Know enough.' to 'See what matters. Skip the spiral.' Same anti-distraction intent, gentler framing.
- Kickstarter pitch (angle 1) revised to lead with what users gain rather than what they fear. Drops 'anti-phone', 'trapdoor', 'screen time saved' framing in favor of 'a calm companion to your phone' angle. Closing line now: 'It's a small, calm surface that lets you skip the spiral when all you needed was a glance.'
- Daily Glancer / Desk Decorator user-class frustrations left as-is — those are authentic user pain points, not marketing voice.

## Misc fixes
- Vite `pngjs` browser stub now uses an actual file (`packages/web/src/stubs/pngjs.ts`) instead of `/dev/null`, so vite build works on Windows (`/dev/null` resolved to `C:\dev\null` and broke).
- Web bundle reads version from package.json at build time via Vite's `define: { __APP_VERSION__: ... }`. Every release auto-stamps the badge.
- Eink display preview SCALE = 1, panel sizes itself to the canvas via CSS vars — bumping SCALE to enlarge the preview is a one-line change.
- Empty-state message in preview canvas: `<Add a box...>` (replaces 'Add a box to see your display').

## Quality gate (committed clean)
- `npm run build` (tsc): pass
- `npm test` (vitest): 74/74 pass
- `npm run lint` (eslint): pass
- `npm run format:check` (prettier): pass

artifacts.title: Round 10 — Counter Pivot (2026-04-22)
artifacts.body:
## What
InfoBento pivots from a dual-display MagSafe clamshell to a single counter-only color eInk decorator. Phone-back use case is gone. MagSafe, hinge, dual-display PCB, kickstand, and the iOS background BLE risk are all removed. Color eInk replaces 1-bit. Solar panel moves to the upper portion of the back side of a monolithic body. Industrial design constrained to white housing, ≤4mm bezel, drop-resistant to 4 feet.

## Why
The user-class fit analysis revealed the clamshell was trying to serve two products at once and paying for it: ~$30 BOM, ~7.2mm thickness, GPIO pressure, hinge sourcing risk, and (most critically) iOS background BLE as a single point of failure that could not be answered before manufacturing capital was committed. The counter device — previously the secondary mode — turns out to be the more de-risked, photogenic, giftable, and Kickstartable product on what we already know. Daily Glancer (the founder) was the user class that justified phone-back; Desk Decorator and Gift Giver are better served by counter-only and were second-class citizens in the dual-display story.

The color upgrade and panel upsize were chosen to differentiate the counter device from monochrome competitors (Tidbyt, generic eInk frames) and to make Kickstarter photography visually striking.

## Decisions made in this round
- Hard pivot: phone-back is gone, not deferred to v2
- Color eInk panel (Spectra 6 or ACeP family, 7-color)
- Larger panel size to be picked from 4.2" / 5.65" / 7.3" candidates in #35
- Drop the kickstand: monolithic body with ~12-15° back-tilt, body-as-stand
- Solar panel mounted on upper portion of back side
- White housing, thin bezel (≤4mm)
- Designed for 4-foot drop survival (bumper layer, edge radius, recessed display)

## Decisions made later in Round 10 (2026-04-22 follow-on session)
- **MCU: ESP32-C3** (Wi-Fi 4 + BLE 5; BLE radio unused in v1, reserved for v2 bridge mode)
- **Connectivity: Wi-Fi direct + PWA-only.** No companion phone app for v1. Web editor at infobento.com is the only configuration surface. Captive-portal first-time setup.

artifacts.title: Round 12 — Box library completion & resilience decisions (2026-04-25)
artifacts.body:
## Implementation landed (v0.11.0 → v0.13.0)

### Fresh-on-fetch box family (4 new box types)
- **Quote** gains optional comma-separated tag steering. Provider switched from zenquotes.io → api.quotable.kurokeita.dev mirror (main quotable.io domain has gone dark — see findings).
- **Horoscope** — 12 zodiac signs, daily reading via api-ninjas (no key required).
- **Joke** — 6 categories (Programming/Misc/Pun/Dark/Spooky/Christmas), safe-mode + blacklist flags always applied. JokeAPI proxy.
- **On This Day** — Wikipedia events/births/deaths/holidays/all for today's UTC date. Server picks one entry randomly so the client never sees the full Wikipedia day payload.

### Editor surface for 5 renderer-only types
stocks, tasks, calendar, habit, worldclock — these had renderers/icons/validation in v0.8.0 but no editor UI. Wired in via a generic list-editor primitive (`buildListField` + `updateConfigList` / `appendToConfigList` / `removeFromConfigList`) used by tasks/calendar/habit/worldclock. Stocks gets a single-input form with debounced auto-fetch.

### Polish
- **Stocks live fetch** via Yahoo Finance proxy (desktop User-Agent required to avoid 429s).
- **Worldclock UTC offset parser** — `UTC+5:30`, `+5`, `-3:30`, etc. Reformats to canonical on blur.
- **Content-aware height for ALL 17 box types** (`computeMinHeight` covers every renderer; previously only quote/horoscope/joke/onthisday). Short-content boxes shrink so list-heavy boxes get the space.
- **BentoConfig.width/height overrides** for non-default panel sizes (gates v2 hardware variants).
- **Deploy gated to v* tag pushes only** (was deploying on every mainline push).

## Decisions

### Q3 — Provider failure resilience
**Bundled local fallback for quote/joke/horoscope only.** ~180KB build artifact total. On API failure for those 3 endpoints, return a random local entry. Other boxes (weather, forecast, on-this-day, stocks, AQI, geocoding) accept `No data` on rare failures — those providers are either robust (Open-Meteo, Wikipedia) or stale data is meaningless (stocks).

Horoscope fallback caveat: bundled set is generic-per-sign (date-agnostic), not today-specific. Acceptable degradation.

### Q4 — First-time-user defaults
**5-box layout, zero config, no wizard:**
1. **[Date | Weather]** merged top row (compact date alongside hero temp)
2. **8-Day Forecast** (full width)
3. **Quote** (full width)
4. **On This Day** (full width)

All input fields empty → auto-fetch on first render. Existing geolocation flow populates city for weather + forecast. Geolocation-denied state shows `Set a location` prompt instead of mock data. New buyers see real data immediately, no fake `Sample task` placeholder copy anywhere.

### Q5 — Account / hosting model
**Hybrid SaaS-default.** Specifics:
- **Pairing:** QR code printed on the device sticker → opens `infobento.com/pair/<code>` on a phone, binds device-id ↔ config.
- **Auth:** passwordless email magic-link. Edit from any browser, no remembered password.
- **Self-host hatch:** device firmware accepts a custom server URL via captive-portal setup. API code is already public; principled buyers fork it.

Reasoning: $5/mo VPS handles 10K devices × 2 fetches/day for years (cost is not the constraint). Real constraint is day-1 UX for the Kickstarter audience — they won't self-host or scan QRs to make config changes. Hybrid keeps the open-source story alive while protecting the masses.

## Implementation backlog from these decisions
- Curate ~200 quotes / ~100 jokes / ~50 horoscopes-per-sign for the fallback bundle (Q3)
- Replace `state.ts:defaultBoxes()` with the curated 5-box layout (Q4) — small
- Build the pairing + magic-link flow on infobento.com: multi-tenant config storage, device-pull API, `/pair/<code>` route, magic-link emailer (Q5) — significant
- Stickered QR generator + device boot-time URL config (Q5, gated on hardware milestone)

artifacts.title: Quotable.io main domain dead — switched to kurokeita.dev mirror
artifacts.description: DNS resolution fails for api.quotable.io as of 2026-04-25. The same dataset is hosted at api.quotable.kurokeita.dev (community fork). Quote provider migrated; tag-steering and maxLength support both work on the mirror. Single-point-of-failure risk: mirror is hobby-hosted.
artifacts.evidence: curl https://api.quotable.io/random returns 'Could not resolve host'; mirror returns expected JSON shape with title-cased tag filtering
artifacts.recommendation: Monitor mirror availability. Round 12 Q3 (bundled local fallback) covers a future failure of the mirror.

artifacts.title: JokeAPI URL hyphen treated as category separator (Knock-Knock unreachable)
artifacts.description: JokeAPI v2 splits the category path segment on hyphens AND commas, so /joke/Knock-Knock is parsed as two categories ('knock', 'knock') and rejected. Knock-Knock is reachable nowhere via the URL scheme. Issue spec listed it as valid; whitelist updated to JokeAPI's actual valid set.
artifacts.evidence: GET /joke/Knock-Knock → 'No matching joke found... Got: knock, knock but possible categories are: Any, Misc, Programming, Dark, Pun, Spooky, Christmas'
artifacts.recommendation: Whitelist limited to: Programming, Misc, Pun, Dark, Spooky, Christmas. Drop Knock-Knock from issue spec going forward.

artifacts.title: Yahoo Finance returns 429 without desktop User-Agent
artifacts.description: query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/<sym> rate-limits anonymous bot traffic; works fine when the request carries a Mozilla-style User-Agent. Stocks proxy adds 'Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; InfoBento/1.0)'.
artifacts.evidence: Bare curl returns 'Edge: Too Many Requests'; with -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' returns expected JSON
artifacts.recommendation: If Yahoo tightens further, stooq.com CSV is a viable no-key fallback (verified working).

artifacts.title: moveBox stripped split-pair markers when reordering across a pair
artifacts.description: moveBox swapped an unpaired box with its neighbor without checking whether the neighbor was part of a split pair. Swapping into a pair left a 'left' or 'right' split marker stranded next to a non-partner, and the box-list render loop's merge-button check (!box.split && !next.split) suppressed merge buttons around the affected boxes — the visible symptom users reported.
artifacts.evidence: User reported merge buttons disappearing after reorder. Reproducible by [unpaired, left, right] → move down on unpaired.
artifacts.recommendation: moveBox now jumps the moving box OVER the entire pair instead of swapping into it. hydrateBoxes also repairs orphaned split markers from previously-corrupted localStorage state.

artifacts.body:
Status snapshot covering everything that landed after the Round 12 implementation note.

## SaaS-default hosting (epic #77) — partially shipped
- **#72 SQLite storage layer** (v0.15.0). `accounts` and `devices` tables in a single SQLite file at `/var/lib/infobento/data.db` (override via `INFOBENTO_DB_PATH`). Helpers for account create/lookup, device pair-code claim (idempotent per account, rejects cross-account claims), config write, per-account device listing. Schema accommodates the planned passkey + OAuth columns without future migration.
- **#73 Passkey + Apple/Google OAuth** (v0.15.0). `@simplewebauthn/server` for WebAuthn (registration + authentication, sign-counter rollback rejection with 0→0 pass-through). `jose` for OIDC + PKCE flows (Sign in with Apple, Google). HMAC-signed session cookies (`{account_id, exp}`, 90-day TTL, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure in production) decoupled from credential type. Stateless 5-minute challenge cookies bridge `/options`↔`/verify` and `/start`↔`/callback` without server-side store. Account upsert surfaces a `linkedToExistingEmail` flag — never silently merges. Seven new auth endpoints: `POST /api/auth/passkey/{register,login}/{options,verify}`, `GET /api/auth/oauth/{apple,google}/{start,callback}`, `POST /api/auth/signout`, `GET /api/auth/session`. Round 12 Q5 originally specified magic-link email auth; the team substituted passkeys + native-IdP OAuth (better UX, no SMTP dependency, broader device coverage).
- **#74 / #75 / #76 — open.** Pair-code claim flow, device-pull config/frame endpoints, web editor account binding remain.

### Self-host env vars (new)
Production deploy now forwards `SESSION_SECRET`, `RP_ID`, `RP_ORIGIN`, `OAUTH_REDIRECT_BASE`, and the Apple/Google OAuth secrets from GitHub secrets to `/etc/infobento/auth.env` (mode 640, root:www-data) for the systemd unit's `EnvironmentFile`. Values omitted from a given run preserve their prior value rather than wiping. README documents the env-var contract and Apple/Google OAuth setup steps for self-hosters. Passkey-only fallback works without any OAuth credentials.

## Box library reshape (v0.16.0)
- **Tasks + World Clock removed** (#84). A device that refreshes once or twice a day can't truthfully show a clock; a checkbox list is overkill on a passive surface. 17 → 15 → 18 net (after horoscope/joke/onthisday). Pre-existing user configs containing `tasks` or `worldclock` will fail Zod validation and render as placeholder boxes. Acceptable break — pre-1.0, single-user product.
- **In-place box type switcher** (#88). Every box-card header now carries a `<select>` that swaps the box's type without disturbing layout. `split` partner, `weight`, `splitRatio`, ordering preserved; `config` reset to new defaults; label overwritten only when it still matches the old default (so user-edited labels survive). New `changeBoxType(id, newType)` action; `LABELS` exported as `BOX_TYPE_LABELS`.
- **Text box honors `\n`** (#84). `drawTextWrapped` and `countWrappedLines` split on explicit newlines first, then word-wrap within each segment. A single Text box now functions as a one-item-per-row list — replaces what the removed Tasks/World Clock boxes did.

## Stocks polish (v0.18.0 → v0.19.0)
- **Duration selector** on every stocks box: `1d` (default), `5d`, `1mo`, `3mo`, `6mo`, `1y`, `5y`. Triggers debounced refetch; change/percent computed against the range's baseline. New `StockDuration` type, `STOCK_DURATIONS` preset list, `DEFAULT_STOCK_DURATION='1d'` exported from `@infobento/core`. `/api/stocks` accepts a `duration` query param mapped to Yahoo `range`/`interval` pairs.
- **Duration shown on the rendered box** — change line appends ` · 1mo` (or current preset) so move magnitude is unambiguous about its time horizon. No suffix when duration unset (preserves the look of older configs).

## Editor polish
- **Landscape preview toggle** (v0.17.0). Preview shows one orientation at a time (portrait by default), swapped by a `Landscape` checkbox. Both PNGs still fetched in one round-trip so the toggle is instant. Replaces the always-on dual-preview layout.
- **Editor cards reflow horizontally** (v0.17.0). Box-config form uses flex-wrap so multi-field forms (date+label, city+entries, etc.) sit side-by-side when there's room. Tighter padding/labels/inputs and a 40px-min textarea (down from 72px) — several boxes fit on screen without scrolling at typical desktop widths.
- **Location-detect button** (v0.20.0). All location fields (weather, forecast, forecast3d, sun, AQI) get a small icon inline with the LOCATION label. One click calls `ipapi.co` (no browser permission required), fills the field, and propagates to other empty location boxes in the layout.
- **Add-box chip rail** (v0.21.0). Replaces the two-step select + `Add Box` button with a wrapping row of pill chips (one per box type, alphabetically). Single click adds.

## Deploy / CI hygiene
- **Deploy gated to `v*` tag pushes only** (v0.13.0). Was deploying on every mainline push.
- **`claude-review` Action `--max-turns` raised 10 → 25** (v0.16.0). Medium PRs (4–5 files across two packages, plus inline comments) routinely needed more than 10.

- v0.16.0 (2026-04-26) — type switcher, text-box \n, tasks/worldclock removed
